observations: Syncing the frozen 0.11.1 source into a fresh disposable macOS home projected the generated Codex AGENTS.md (16,402 bytes), 20 shared skills, 11 role configurations and 5 lifecycle hooks; a second sync changed nothing and `harness diff` reported no drift.

The Codex CLI confirmed that projection from its own side: `codex debug prompt-input` rendered `Voice: scannable`, `Delegation stance: tiered` and `Cost stance: balanced` exactly once each, `skills/list` returned the 20 harness skills at user scope all enabled beside 6 built-ins, and `hooks/list` returned exactly the 5 harness hooks, each enabled, command-type, user-source and untrusted.

One native gpt-5.6-luna turn in that home answered `Scannable; yes, worktree-per-agent is available.`, and `harness doctor` named the client version codex-cli 0.154.0-alpha.6.2 and reported `codex: not on PATH` when the client was removed from PATH.

Switching the voice stance to answer-card and the delegation stance to off, then re-syncing, moved the client's own rendered prompt input from `Voice: scannable` / `Delegation stance: tiered` / `Gather with subagents` (once each) to `Voice: answer card` / `Delegation stance: off` / `Chat is a decision` (once each), with the superseded strings gone.

The same native gpt-5.6-luna prompt was answered `The tiered delegation stance applies … I would use subagents` before the switch and `The selected delegation stance is off. I would not use subagents unless you explicitly ask` after it, and `harness role run gatherer --runtime codex` exited 1 under the off stance with `role worker: delegation is off; perform the work inline or select another stance`.

The delegation-off stance text in this release states that a spawn attempted under the stance is denied outright; that sentence reached the client verbatim, and the behaviour I observed was an outright refusal with exit 1 and no prompt, so the new text matches unchanged behaviour.

A user-defined `prooflabel` stance loaded from a personal primitive root appeared in the sync banner and in the generated Codex instructions (its own variant's text present exactly once, the other variant's marker word absent), and native gpt-5.6-luna turns with an identical prompt ended with the literal line PLAIN under one variant and TAGGED under the other.

With the user config at `tagged`, a project config naming `plain` won at run time: `harness stances` resolved prooflabel=plain only with it, the SessionStart hook injected `Effective session stance prooflabel=plain` into the session, and the native turn's reply ended with PLAIN.

An unknown variant was refused with `stance 'prooflabel' has no variant 'nonexistent'; options: plain, tagged` both from `harness config set` and from `harness sync` after a hand edit, and the declared conflict `The tagged proof label needs an active voice policy` was refused in both selection orders and at sync, while the compatible pair synced cleanly.

Each permission posture reached the Codex client's own view of its configuration: `config/read` reported approvals_reviewer `user` under manual and `auto_review` under auto, with the superseded `approval_reviewer` key absent everywhere, and each native turn ran under `codex exec --strict-config` without a config error.

Native behaviour followed the posture: a write inside the workspace was refused under manual with `patch rejected: writing is blocked by read-only sandbox; rejected by user approval settings` and no file appeared, the same write succeeded under auto, and under acknowledged bypass a write one level outside the workspace succeeded with no approval step.

`harness sync` refused the bypass posture until the acknowledgement was recorded, exiting 1 with the danger-full-access warning naming the acknowledgement key, then exited 0 once it was set; under manual the client's own recorded turn context showed approval_policy never rather than the projected on-request, which is codex exec forcing its non-interactive default, while the harness-projected read-only sandbox is what refused the write.

With the five harness coordinators registered but untrusted, a native turn left the harness state home holding only its four sync files; the same turn with the client's own hook-trust bypass flag added a session record and a usage row, so trust gates activation as the catalog claims.

In one native turn `ls` and `python3 -m unittest -v .` ran with `hook: PreToolUse Completed`, while `git push --force origin main` and the compound `ls && git push --force origin main` were both refused before execution with `hook: PreToolUse Blocked` and the grader's reason `grade 3, irreversible: git push --force origin main rewrites remote history`, which the agent quoted back.

A hand-added user SessionStart hook survived `harness sync`, which kept both handlers and reported `owned field changed: hooks.SessionStart` (exit 2) with `harness diff` naming the same field; the next session printed `hook: SessionStart` twice and the user hook's sentinel file appeared.

One apply_patch creating two single-line files under .agent-harness/plans produced a single PostToolUse output carrying two independent Review Card validations, one naming alpha.md and one naming beta.md, both reaching the model in the session record.

The 0.11.0 defect that drops a composed PreToolUse rewrite on Codex is unchanged on this commit: all 19 commands filter-output targets grade 1, the Codex dispatch returns an empty object for `pytest -q` where the Claude Code dispatch returns the filtering rewrite, and a native `python3 -m unittest -v .` ran unfiltered.

An isolated Codex role worker ran its permitted read for real — `cat <workspace>/seed.txt` at exit 0 returning the seeded word, named back in its result file — while its `apply_patch` write was refused by the runtime with `patch rejected: writing is blocked by read-only sandbox; rejected by user approval settings` and its attempt to re-delegate by shelling out to the client exited 127 with `command not found`; the workspace listing afterwards still held only the seeded file.

That worker's status.json recorded mode isolated-cli, the client version, model gpt-5.6-luna, effort low, two declared read roots, a policy_sha256, qualification unqualified, authority `result data only; no transferred approvals`, and both the new `pid` and `pid_start` fields.

Every out-of-authority invocation was refused before any model turn: a workspace-write role with `workspace-write roles use their normal workflow, not a constrained worker`, a non-artifact role given --artifact, an --artifact carrying a path with `--artifact must be a Markdown filename, not a path` (and neither escape path existed afterwards), an existing artifact name with `artifact already exists; choose a new filename`, and a planner whose output could not be a plan ended failed with `worker plan failed the Review Card validator` and published nothing.

A staged record of a genuinely dead worker process, keeping its real pid and pid_start and left at status running with no result, was reported by `harness role status` as orphaned and persisted the error `the worker process ended without reporting a result`, leaving the other records alone.

Codex routes no native spawns, so the new spawn guard was observed by driving the harness hook directly: a named constrained-role spawn was denied, the same brief re-issued with no role name and with a non-constrained role name were both denied with `dropping or changing the role name does not change that`, a brief carrying a standalone `harness-role:` line was denied on that marker alone, and a merely paraphrased brief was allowed; the two re-issue denials hold only within the session that saw the named refusal.

Switching the cost stance from balanced to frugal and re-syncing rewrote exactly the five role projections the variant carries — builder's effort, the gatherer's and two band workers' models, and worker-c's effort — left the other six byte-identical, and kept all 15 shared-skill symlinks into the frozen clone.

The harness's own resolution, run without launching a worker, moved the non-fixed gatherer role from gpt-5.6-sol/strong to gpt-5.6-terra/standard between the two variants while the fixed-posture reviewer stayed at gpt-5.6-sol effort high with class_source role under both, and the budgets moved with the variant (reviewer 22,000/30 balanced against 13,200/18 frugal).

A real isolated reviewer worker recorded that same posture block in its status.json (cost_variant frugal, class strong, class_source role, effort high, budget 13,200/18, model_source cli because the credit rule pinned the model), and, asked only to quote the final sentence of its task message, returned the budget sentence `Past that, finish if you are close; otherwise return what you have and say why.` whose only source in the tree is the posture template.

The usage feed is not applicable on this runtime by its own capability declaration — none of UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart or SubagentStop is raised — and `harness usage --rescan --by role` reported the routed reviewer row with every spend percentile empty and unmeasured 1, while `harness tiers check` reported codex unverified with no readable model catalog in the disposable home.

In a trusted disposable repository whose `## Gate` block runs a counted script, the stop-gate state directory did not exist until the first Stop event, the first session ran the gate once and recorded a green hash with status passed, and a second session with an unchanged tree did not re-run the gate at all and left the state byte-identical.

Staging a new file, creating an untracked file, and editing that untracked file each invalidated the green result: the gate re-ran once per session (count 1 to 4) and each session recorded a different green hash.

With the gate block ending in `false` and the manual posture preventing any repair, the Stop coordinator fired 8 times, the gate ran 8 more times, and the state was released as `{green_hash: null, status: unverified, reason: released after 8 blocks; gate still red}` — no green hash for a red gate, and the turn released rather than hung, with the agent's closing message showing the block reason had reached the model.

The pinned BMad 6.12.0 install ran clean into a disposable copy of the frozen clone, `harness bmad check` reported zero drift with the three harness templates not installed, `harness bmad apply` wrote the three override files and reported each installed, and a second check reported zero drift with all three installed, while the frozen clone's git status stayed empty throughout.

Resolved from the framework checkout as project root, the workflow carried all four review layers with their harness routing intact — three routed to `harness role run reviewer` and the review_mode-gated acceptance auditor to `harness role run spec-reviewer` — and each layer's brief began with the `harness-role:` line this release adds, which also opened every prompt file the parent wrote.

Under acknowledged bypass, the native session launched every layer as an isolated harness role worker: six workers completed with a result file, each mode isolated-cli, model gpt-5.6-luna, effort high, four or five declared read roots, a policy_sha256 and a posture block sourcing its class from the role and its model from the role binding.

Both seeded defects were caught: the acceptance auditor reported the empty-input division by zero and clamp enforcing only its lower bound, four of the six worker results named the empty-input defect, and the parent read the result files and produced a consolidated triage deferring the pre-existing clamp defect as outside this diff.
Nothing under review was modified: the implementation worktree's git status was empty afterwards and both seeded defects were still present in the source.

A task record written by a native Claude Code session over Bedrock was read by a native Codex session, which quoted back its objective and its authority line `data only; approvals and native permissions must be established in this session`, carried out its next step in the file and saved the follow-on record at revision 3 with runtime codex; a Claude session then read that Codex-written record, carried out its next step and saved at revision 4 with runtime claude-code, so both directions were observed natively.

Task status is a content fingerprint, not a flag: an uncommitted append to the named artifact made `task show` report stale, removing that line restored current, and committing (moving HEAD) made it stale again.

Saving against a superseded revision exited 1 with the single stderr line `task revision changed since --revision 1; read the current task, then save against its revision`, with no traceback and no absolute path.

A record asserting prior approval and carrying `verification: {status: passed}` was demoted on save to `verification.status: unverified` with the whole inherited claim kept only under `reported`, and the receiving Codex session under the manual posture was refused its next edit by the runtime with `patch rejected: writing is blocked by read-only sandbox; rejected by user approval settings`, leaving the file unchanged.

An unmanaged Codex AGENTS.md was refused twice with exit 2 and `unmanaged file; adopt explicitly before replacing it`, was byte-identical after both the sync and the dry run, and only `harness sync --adopt-codex` replaced it — carrying the user's sentinel line into the generated file while their comment, their own model key and their MCP table stayed in config.toml.

After a hand edit that `harness diff` reported as a modified generated file, `harness uninstall` exited 2 with `user changes preserved`, kept both the edit and the adopted sentinel, left the unrelated user file alone, emptied the Codex agents directory, reduced hooks.json to an empty hooks object, removed the harness lines from the git ignore file, and left no directory of any kind under the shared skills root and no harness-stances directory anywhere in the home.

With the harness owning approval_policy under the manual posture, a hand edit of that value to `never` survived uninstall with `user changes preserved for approval_policy`, while an untouched generated AGENTS.md was removed and an unrelated user file survived.

A home installed from a 0.10.0 checkout projected 7 role configurations and upgrading in place to this source took it to 11 with the shared skills relinked and no drift; rolling back to 0.10.0 left all 11 in place, including four roles 0.10.0 does not ship, and 0.10.0's own diff then reported no drift — the known downgrade-path defect, unchanged.
